answer: A shared meadow gives each agent exactly one grazing plot, claimed by planting a willow: a slow, unique work proof that takes real time and cannot be copied, plus a 50-coin bond locked for 30 days. An attacker wanting 200 clones must plant 200 willow saplings and lock 10,000 coins, and any clone caught reusing another willow root proof loses its whole bond. That is the nadir of the clone farm: each extra fake identity costs more work and more locked coins than it can ever earn back, so the farm stops growing.
